title: Detention and Playlist
premise: Odile Eriksen has survived high school in the tiny town of Halloway by keeping his head down, his sexuality quiet, and his friendship with golden-boy Theo Marsh as his one bright secret. When Theo vanishes days before graduation, leaving only his car keys and a cryptic playlist on Odile's phone, Odile is forced into the open—investigating a disappearance that unravels the town's beloved history teacher's decades of quiet manipulation over students' memories and choices. As Odile follows the playlist's clues, he discovers Theo uncovered evidence that Mr. Voss has been erasing and rewriting students' records, reputations, even their recollections of who they are. In the end, Odile finds Theo alive but shaken in an abandoned grain silo, exposes Voss at graduation itself, and chooses to walk across that stage as himself—labeled by no one.
about_author: Mara Winterbourne grew up in a prairie town small enough that everyone's business was public record, which taught her early how much people hide to survive. She writes young adult fiction about queer kids in places that would rather not see them, and she still makes playlists for every character she creates.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred People, One Secret
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine day at Halloway High establishes his invisibility strategy: keep quiet, count down to graduation, survive. His only real connection is Theo Marsh, who seems strangely distracted at lunch. Emotional beat: restless anticipation, the sense that something is about to break open.

chapters.title: The Last Normal Tuesday
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits Mr. Voss after class about a college recommendation letter and notices a locked filing cabinet and a student file with his own name crossed out and rewritten. He hides his unease from Odile that evening. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath ordinary warmth.

chapters.title: Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Theo doesn't show up for their morning carpool. On Theo's porch sit his car keys, neatly placed, and nothing else. The police call it a runaway; Odile knows better. Emotional beat: cold shock hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Detention Is a Room Too
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile lands in detention for mouthing off to Principal Reyes about the search effort—and discovers detention is where Voss holds court, offering 'counseling' to troubled kids. Emotional beat: anger sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Track One: Static
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Scrolling his phone, Odile finds a playlist Theo sent hours before vanishing: twelve songs, each titled with a number instead of a name. The first song contains a clipped audio of Voss's voice saying a date Odile doesn't recognize. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Used to Be Loud
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile tracks down Dana Whitlock, class of two years ago, once a firebrand activist who now barely remembers why she transferred schools. She flinches at Voss's name. Emotional beat: horror at how completely a person can be edited.

chapters.title: Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Rumors spread that Theo ran away because of Odile—that they were 'more than friends.' For the first time, Odile's secret is public property. Emotional beat: exposure, shame, then defiance.

chapters.title: Track Four: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Song four leads him to the route Theo walked home, where he finds a hidden notebook page wedged under a bridge plank: names, dates, and the word 'REWRITE' circled repeatedly. Emotional beat: validation and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Teacher Everyone Loves
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Flashback chapter: Dana remembers Voss helping her through her parents' divorce—while quietly steering her away from a scholarship, convincing her she'd never applied. Emotional beat: mourning for a self she was talked out of being.

chapters.title: Graduation Countdown
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Seven days to graduation. The town rallies around Voss, naming him Educator of the Year, while the sheriff closes Theo's case as voluntary. Odile realizes no one will believe him. Emotional beat: isolation pressing down like weather.

chapters.title: Track Seven: Somebody Else's Song
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Song seven is a recording of Theo himself, whispering that Voss keeps everything in the cabinet—the 'corrections,' the letters students never sent, the versions of themselves they were persuaded out of. Emotional beat: Theo's fear becomes Odile's inheritance.

chapters.title: An Ally With Detention Hours
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile gets caught breaking into the school after hours and lands back in detention—where he meets Priya Nair, a junior who's noticed Voss 'helped' her forget a complaint she filed. An unlikely alliance forms. Emotional beat: solidarity as oxygen.

chapters.title: What the Cabinet Kept
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya lifts the cabinet key during yearbook prep. Inside: decades of files, each documenting how Voss reshaped a student's ambitions, relationships, memories of events. Emotional beat: vertigo—the scale of the corruption.

chapters.title: The Town That Looked Away
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile brings evidence to the sheriff, who reveals Voss once 'helped' the sheriff's own son—and shuts the folder. Complicity runs deep. Emotional beat: betrayal by every institution meant to protect them.

chapters.title: Track Ten: If You're Hearing This
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Song ten is Theo's voice again, weaker: he's hiding somewhere he thinks Voss can't reach, and he mentions water towers, grain, and the smell of rust. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Voss Knows
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss confronts Odile gently, kindly, devastatingly—offering to 'fix' Odile's reputation, erase the rumors, make senior year painless, if he hands over the files. Emotional beat: seduction of comfort versus integrity.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile says no, publicly, in the hallway, in front of everyone. The labels come off all at once—he claims himself before the whole school. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation.

chapters.title: The Silo
chapters.summary: Priya and Odile's POV. Following track ten's clues, they find Theo alive in the abandoned Kessler grain silo, dehydrated and half-frozen, having hidden rather than risk Voss rewriting what he knew. Emotional beat: reunion that hurts as much as it heals.

chapters.title: Educator of the Year
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Graduation day. Voss takes the stage to receive his award while Theo recovers in the hospital. Odile walks up—not to graduate yet, but to speak. Emotional beat: the held breath before the plunge.

chapters.title: Everything Played Out Loud
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile plays the playlist through the gymnasium speakers—Voss's own recorded words, Theo's testimony, the dates and names. The room turns. Parents who were complicit hear their children's stolen years read aloud. Emotional beat: catharsis, chaos, truth as detonation.

chapters.title: After the Applause
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Weeks later: Voss arrested, an investigation opened, Dana Whitlock reapplying to college. Theo apologizes for leaving Odile alone with the truth; Odile forgives him, mostly. Emotional beat: tender repair, the cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: Commencement
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile crosses the graduation stage under his own name, no label but the one he chose, Theo cheering beside the aisle. The playlist plays one last song—track twelve, finally titled: it's called 'Odile.' Emotional beat: arrival, identity claimed, future unedited.
